title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: The Chowchilla Bus Kidnapping
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck (with a co-host credited as iHeart Intro in the transcript) cover the 1976 Chowchilla school bus kidnapping in California. On July 15, 1976, driver Ed Ray and 26 children were hijacked in a van, driven about eleven hours, and buried alive in a moving van trailer at a rock quarry in Livermore. Fourteen-year-old Mike Marshall led the escape after about 12 hours; Ed Ray and the children were found at the quarry. The episode covers the frenzy in Chowchilla, the kidnappers Fred Woods, James Schoenfeld and Richard Schoenfeld, their sloppy planning, their capture within about two weeks, the court ruling on bodily harm, parole of the brothers, Woods' continued imprisonment, the victims' lasting trauma, a 1993 Lifetime movie, and a listener mail segment on racially biased traffic ticketing. Includes a long tangent about personal anecdotes and the Air Supply concert and a song about the kidnapping by Robert Goulet (transcript spells it Goolay).

segments.title: Cold open
segments.summary: Josh introduces the 1976 Chowchilla bus kidnapping, in which 26 children and their driver were buried alive while kidnappers waited for ransom.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts greet listeners and banter about a song and a band name before introducing the topic and how Josh's aunt remembers the case.

segments.title: Setting the scene in Chowchilla
segments.summary: Description of the small town of Chowchilla in the San Joaquin Valley and the July 15, 1976 summer school field trip. Bus driver Ed Ray, a farmer and school bus driver, was carrying children home.

segments.title: Mike Marshall boards the bus
segments.summary: Fourteen-year-old Mike Marshall, punished by his mother, was not supposed to be on the bus and asked Ed Ray for a ride home. The hijacking began when Ray turned onto Avenue 21 and found a van blocking the road.

segments.title: 1993 movie mention
segments.summary: Hosts mention a Lifetime movie from the 1990s starring Karl Malden as Ed Ray, and a joke about his reluctance to leave the driver's seat.

segments.title: Transfer to vans
segments.summary: The kidnappers forced the bus to be driven under their van escort, then moved the children to two vans. The vans were fitted with plywood partitions and painted windows and drove for eleven hours with no food, water or bathroom breaks.

segments.title: Arrival at the quarry
segments.summary: Around 3:30 am Friday the vans reached a rock quarry in Livermore, about 100 miles from Chowchilla, where a moving van trailer had been buried 12 feet underground under four feet of dirt.

segments.title: Captivity underground
segments.summary: The kidnappers recorded the children's names and parents' phone numbers on a Jack in the Box wrapper and took clothing from each child to use as proof for ransom. The trailer had limited food, water, bathrooms and ventilation, and mattresses and box springs.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break.

segments.title: Search and media frenzy in Chowchilla
segments.summary: The bus was found hidden with bamboo and camouflage but had no clues. Sheriff Ed Gates requested help; the FBI and state agencies came, and national media descended. Rumors about the Zodiac killer and a 1958 novel were investigated. Families gathered at the firehouse. The kids were found about 32 hours later when they presented themselves to a quarry security guard.

segments.title: The escape from the trailer
segments.summary: The roof began to cave in under the weight of dirt and batteries. Mike Marshall reportedly led the escape, with Ed Ray helping; Larry Park's book corroborated this. Hosts discuss how Ray was later considered a hero and remained in Chowchilla.

segments.title: Breaking out and rescue
segments.summary: The kids pried open the roof using wood from a box spring, climbed out, and Mike Marshall checked for the kidnappers. No one was there, and the group was found by a quarry security guard. Ed Ray was hailed as a hero.

segments.title: Trauma and aftermath for the children
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the heat, dehydration and fear the children endured, and the danger of the roof collapsing. The FBI and sheriff interviewed the children; a Greyhound bus returned them to Chowchilla. Donations from Pacific Bell and others were made.

segments.title: Disneyland, a ballad, and off-topic tangents
segments.summary: The children were honored with a parade and a Disneyland trip. Ed Ray appeared on Hollywood Squares. Robert Goulet recorded a song about the kidnapping, and the hosts discuss it and Air Supply and Goulet's TV-shooting habit.

segments.title: The kidnappers' backgrounds
segments.summary: Ringleader Fred Woods (Frederick Newhall Woods IV), from a wealthy California family, and the brothers James and Richard Schoenfeld, who were both Eagle Scouts, planned the crime. Woods had a family fortune, neglectful parents, and a desire to be a film producer. James wanted money to keep up with neighbors. Woods worked at his father's quarry.

segments.title: Motives and the state budget surplus
segments.summary: The kidnappers reasoned that California had a budget surplus and insurance would cover a $5 million ransom if the children were on a school bus. Their lack of morality and failure to consider psychological harm are discussed.

segments.title: Lasting trauma and town response
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the random selection of Chowchilla and the town's reluctance to process trauma. Victims later faced addiction, nightmares and PTSD. In 2015 a reporter asked Richard Schoenfeld about trauma.

segments.title: Ransom plan, flight and capture
segments.summary: The kidnappers left a ransom note with misspellings and claimed to be a satanic group. The ransom phone lines were jammed. Woods fled to Vancouver under the alias Ralph Snyder and was arrested after writing letters. Richard Schoenfeld confessed; James tried to cross into Canada and was arrested on an all-points bulletin.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break.

segments.title: Sentencing, appeal and parole
segments.summary: Courts initially ruled the kidnappers caused bodily harm, allowing life without parole, but a 1980 appeals court reversed that. Richard Schoenfeld was paroled around 2015 after about 37 to 39 years; James in 2012. Fred Woods has been denied parole 17 times, ran businesses from prison, and was sued by victims in 2016. Larry Park forgave the perpetrators.

segments.title: Movie and further reading
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the 1993 Lifetime film, shot in Kansas, which Chowchilla residents disliked, and recommend a Vox article on the kidnapping.

segments.title: Listener mail: racist ticketing
segments.summary: Listener Valerie Mates of Ann Arbor, Michigan wrote about traffic camera tickets in Chicago, saying the disparity comes from how neighborhoods are designed, with fewer traffic-calming features in poorer areas.

segments.title: Listener mail sign-off
segments.summary: Josh asks listeners to send brainbuster emails.

segments.title: Outro
segments.summary: Show credits and iHeartRadio promotion.
